blocks.text: India's **industrial policy** shifted from the **licence-permit Raj** to **liberalisation (1991)** and now to **manufacturing-led initiatives** — **Make in India, PLI schemes, Start-up & Stand-up India** — aiming to raise the manufacturing share and generate jobs.

rows: Basis of the public-sector-led 'mixed economy'; three schedules of industries.
**Abolished licensing (mostly), reduced public-sector reservation, allowed FDI** — LPG.
Boost manufacturing to **25% of GDP**; 25 sectors; ease of doing business.
**Start-up India (2016)** — innovation/funding; **Stand-up India** — loans for SC/ST & women entrepreneurs.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: industrial policy & Make in India

items: **Industrial policy evolution**: **IPR 1948 & 1956** (mixed economy, 'commanding heights' to PSUs, licensing) → **1991 New Industrial Policy** (delicensing, dereservation, disinvestment, FDI opened).

**Make in India (2014)**: boost manufacturing to **25% of GDP**; 25 sectors; Ease of Doing Business; **PLI (Production-Linked Incentive)** schemes across 14 sectors (electronics, pharma, semiconductors, etc.); Gati Shakti (logistics), National Logistics Policy.

**Start-up India (2016)** & **Stand-Up India (2016)**: startup ecosystem (India = 3rd-largest startup/unicorn hub), tax holidays, Fund of Funds (SIDBI); Stand-Up = bank loans for SC/ST & women entrepreneurs.
**MSMEs**: the backbone — ~30% of GDP, largest employer after agriculture; **Udyam** registration; credit guarantee (CGTMSE), MUDRA.
**Atmanirbhar Bharat (2020)**: self-reliance, PLI, defence indigenisation.
IPR 1956 (public-sector-led) → IPR 1991 (liberalisation) → Make in India (2014).
PLI = production-linked incentives; Stand-up India = SC/ST & women loans.

sections.heading: SEZs, industrial corridors, energy & power policies

blocks.text: To drive industry, India promotes **Special Economic Zones (SEZs), industrial corridors, and energy/power reforms** — expanding infrastructure and renewable capacity to meet growing demand and climate goals.

rows: **SEZ Act (2005)** — duty-free enclaves for exports; single-window; e.g. many in AP/coast.
**Electricity Act (2003)**; unbundling; **UDAY** (discom finances); One Nation One Grid.
Target **500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030**; solar (ISA), wind; National Solar Mission.
Coal (dominant), oil imports, **National Green Hydrogen Mission, ethanol blending**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: SEZs, corridors & energy

items: **SEZs (SEZ Act 2005)**: duty-free enclaves for exports (single-window, tax breaks); India's first was **Kandla EPZ (1965)**; concerns — land, revenue loss, jobs.
**Industrial corridors**: **DMIC (Delhi-Mumbai), CBIC (Chennai-Bengaluru), Vizag-Chennai (VCIC) through AP, Amritsar-Kolkata, Bengaluru-Mumbai**; anchored by **PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan**.

**Energy/power**: sources — coal (~50%+ of power), hydro, nuclear, and fast-growing **renewables (solar, wind)**; targets — **500 GW non-fossil by 2030, 50% energy from renewables, Net-Zero 2070**; **ISA, National Solar Mission, Green Hydrogen Mission, PM-KUSUM (solar farms), PM Surya Ghar (rooftop solar)**.
**Power-sector reforms**: Electricity Act 2003, UDAY (DISCOM revival), One Nation One Grid, RE parks (AP has large solar/wind capacity).
SEZ Act 2005 (export enclaves); corridors (DMIC, VCIC); Electricity Act 2003 + UDAY.
Renewables target 500 GW non-fossil by 2030; Green Hydrogen Mission.

blocks.text: The **1991 economic reforms**, triggered by a **balance-of-payments crisis**, launched **Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation (LPG)** — dismantling controls, opening to foreign capital and trade, and setting India on a high-growth path.

rows: **1991 BoP/forex crisis** (gold pledged); PM **P.V. Narasimha Rao**, FM **Manmohan Singh**.
**Abolished licensing, freed prices, reduced tariffs, deregulated interest rates**.
**FDI/FII, current-account convertibility, WTO integration, export orientation**.
**Higher growth, foreign investment, services boom**; but inequality & farm-sector concerns.

items: **Trigger**: 1991 **Balance-of-Payments crisis** (forex for ~2 weeks, gold pledged); **Narasimha Rao–Manmohan Singh** reforms + IMF conditionalities.
**Liberalisation**: abolition of **industrial licensing** (except a few), **MRTP** eased, dereservation, interest-rate & trade liberalisation.
**Privatisation**: **disinvestment** of PSU equity, strategic sales, **PSU reform** (Maharatna/Navratna autonomy); recent **National Monetisation Pipeline & Asset Monetisation**.
**Globalisation**: rupee devaluation & later convertibility (current-account), **FDI/FII opening**, tariff cuts, **WTO membership (1995)**, integration into global value chains.
**Outcome**: higher growth (services/IT boom), forex build-up, poverty decline — but inequality, agrarian & informal-sector stress; **second-generation reforms** (GST, IBC, labour codes) followed.
1991 BoP crisis → LPG (Rao-Manmohan); liberalisation (delicensing), privatisation (disinvestment), globalisation (FDI/trade).
Rupee devalued; new industrial & trade policy 1991.

sections.heading: International trade, Balance of Payments & India–WTO

blocks.text: **International trade** connects India to the world economy. The **Balance of Payments (BoP)** records all external transactions, and the **WTO** governs the rules of global trade — an arena where India defends its farmers and developing-country interests.

rows: **Exports – imports**; India runs a **trade deficit** (esp. crude oil, gold).
Succeeded **GATT**; HQ **Geneva**; agreements on goods (GATT), services (GATS), IP (TRIPS), agriculture (AoA).
Defends **MSP/public stockholding (peace clause), farmer subsidies**; opposes rich-country farm subsidies.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: trade, BoP & WTO

items: **Balance of Payments (BoP)**: **Current Account** (trade in goods+services, income, transfers/remittances — India has a **trade deficit** but large **services surplus & remittances**, world's top remittance recipient) + **Capital Account** (FDI, FPI, loans); India keeps **capital-account controls**.
**Forex reserves** (RBI-managed, among world's largest ~$600bn+); rupee is **market-determined/managed float**.
**Trade policy**: Foreign Trade Policy (DGFT), export promotion (SEZs, schemes replacing MEIS → **RoDTEP**), FTAs (UAE-CEPA, Australia-ECTA), 'Vocal for Local'.

**WTO (1995, Geneva)**: successor to **GATT**; principles — MFN, National Treatment; India's stances — **agriculture subsidies/food security ('peace clause'), public stockholding, patents (TRIPS & generic medicines), e-commerce moratorium**; disputes via the (currently stalled) Appellate Body.
BoP = current + capital account; India runs a trade deficit (oil & gold imports).
WTO (1995) agreements: GATT/GATS/TRIPS/AoA; India defends food-security stockholding.

prelimsPointers: **Balance of Payments** = **Current Account** (goods, services, transfers) + **Capital Account** (FDI, FII, loans).
